name: Tadalafil ED integrated trials
question: Does as-needed tadalafil improve erectile function compared with placebo in men with erectile dysfunction?

design.population: 1,112 men aged 22–82 years with mild to severe erectile dysfunction of varied etiologies across five trials; eligibility required at least four intercourse attempts during a four-week treatment-free run-in, and men who failed to achieve an erection after radical prostatectomy or pelvic surgery were excluded.
design.description: Integrated analysis of five double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trials

verdictNote: All three co-primary outcomes favored tadalafil at 20 mg versus placebo.
takeaway: Across five placebo-controlled trials, as-needed tadalafil 20 mg improved IIEF erectile-function scores and both SEP co-primary outcomes versus placebo over 12 weeks; the GAQ found improved erections in 81% of 165 men versus 35% of 261 controls in four trials.

reports.label: Five-trial integrated analysis
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give October 2002, without a day
reports.citation: Brock GB, McMahon CG, Chen KK, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of Tadalafil for the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction: Results of Integrated Analyses." *J Urol.* 2002;168(4 Pt 1):1332-1336. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)64442-4

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12-week endpoint, 20-mg tadalafil versus placebo (intent-to-treat efficacy set)
results.note: Adjusted pairwise P value; confidence interval and endpoint-specific analysis denominators not reported.

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12-week endpoint in proportion of yes responses to penetration attempts, 20-mg tadalafil versus placebo (intent-to-treat efficacy set)
results.note: Adjusted pairwise P value; confidence interval and endpoint-specific attempt denominators not reported.

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12-week endpoint in proportion of yes responses to successful intercourse attempts, 20-mg tadalafil versus placebo (intent-to-treat efficacy set)
results.note: Primary outcome is mean patient-level SEP-Q3 change; the 75% versus 32% absolute proportion of all attempts is secondary. Confidence interval and endpoint-specific attempt denominators not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1333–1334; Table 3; Results, p 1334

results.measure: Men reporting improved erections at endpoint in four 12-week studies, 20-mg tadalafil versus placebo
results.note: Four-study GAQ analysis; response numerators and confidence interval not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and footnote; Results, p 1335

results.endpoint: Sexual Encounter Profile question 3, all attempts
results.measure: Absolute proportion of all intercourse attempts successfully completed during treatment, 20-mg tadalafil versus placebo
results.note: Attempt-level secondary outcome; attempt denominators, confidence interval and endpoint-specific P value not reported.

results.measure: Proportion with IIEF erectile-function domain score at least 26 at 12-week endpoint, 20-mg tadalafil versus placebo
results.note: Endpoint-specific denominators and confidence interval not reported.

delivery.label: Treatment schedule
delivery.value: Fixed as-needed tadalafil doses of 2.5, 5, 10, or 20 mg, up to once daily, without food, alcohol, or sexual-activity timing restrictions; placebo control. At 20 mg, 73%–80% of intercourse attempts at selected intervals from 30 minutes to 36 hours after dosing were successful.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1333; Results, p 1335; Erratum, J Urol. 2005;173:664

delivery.label: Treatment completion
delivery.value: 995/1,112 (89%) completed treatment; efficacy required a baseline and at least one post-baseline measurement, and safety included all randomized men.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, p 1333
delivery.note: One constituent study extended to 24 weeks, but the integrated efficacy analysis used 12-week data.
